properties.statement:
ELEVEN THINGS TWO EXTERNAL SESSIONS SAID WORKED, RECORDED BECAUSE A REGRESSION IN ANY OF THEM WOULD OTHERWISE BE INVISIBLE. Both reporters wrote these deliberately — the usgov session titled its section 'Small things that went right, recorded so they don't get regressed'. `fact_type` is `field_confirmation` rather than `defect`: the field is free-form and indexed by design (`dec:defects-are-temporal-facts`), and a design that only records what broke cannot tell a capability that still works from one nobody has exercised.

═══ FROM ALEX'S GROK 4.6 SESSION, 2026-08-14 (docs/feedback/2026-08-14-alex-grok-session.md) ═══

1. CAPTURE-BEFORE-BUILD PAID OFF, which is the product's central claim: 'The graph held enough settled Decisions that the first implementation pass did not invent the verb, the daily cap, viewed-on-scroll, or topic list. That is the point of capture-before-build and it worked.'
2. `compare_designs` against the committed export at session start 'was honest: live graph was already ahead. Better than guessing from counts.'
3. `record_change` SNAPSHOTS SURVIVED THE GATE BEING REWRITTEN THREE TIMES — 'a later reader can see the swing without git archaeology' — with his own qualifier attached: 'when the snapshot was taken BEFORE the merge'.
4. `add_change_event`'s refusal NAMED THE LEGAL VALUES when he passed an unknown one. 'Actionable error.' That is `req:a-refusal-names-what-would-have-worked` observed in the field.
5. `link_artifact` + checksum closed `unrealized_capability`, and he ran the right check — confirming the capability had left that gap's `affected_ids` rather than watching the total, 'as the skill warns'.
6. `search_design` 'still the right way to find the gate Requirement / Decision when the user describes a bug in their words'.

═══ FROM THE US-GOVERNMENT GENESIS SESSION, 2026-08-15 (docs/feedback/2026-08-15-usgov-genesis-session.md, item 5) ═══

7. BATCH FAILURE REPORTING: `create_nodes` 'listing EVERY failure rather than the first, and writing nothing, made a 32-node batch safe to attempt'. The all-or-nothing contract is what made the retry cheap.
8. `describe_schema {from, to}` RANKING MODELLED PAIRS ABOVE WILDCARD ONES: 'ALLOCATED_TO was found in one call.' Same mechanism that this session used to prove `link_artifact` was accepting a Requirement by accident.
9. `Requirement.source` AND `provenance` BEING SEPARATE FIELDS: source carried the citation ('US Const. art. I, sec. 7, cl. 2'), provenance carried whether a human stated it or a model inferred it. 'The user explicitly asked to be able to tell those apart later, and the schema already supported it.'
10. ⭐ `CONTRADICTS` WITH `alignment: opposing|supporting` — called 'THE SINGLE MOST VALUABLE THING reflow2 gave this model'. It let live constitutional tensions (War Powers Resolution vs Commander in Chief; nondelegation) be first-class content 'instead of prose buried in a description'.
11. The `gap_to_prompt` TWO-STEP HANDSHAKE 'produced better questions than were put in, and records them so a later session does not re-ask'.

WHAT THIS IS EVIDENCE FOR, stated carefully: eleven behaviours worked for two independent users on two domains, one of which contains no software. WHAT IT IS NOT: a claim that any of them is verified — a user saying a thing worked is an observation, not a passing check, and several of these have no Verification behind them at all.
